version.changelog:
Self Updater 1.2.0 introduces AI-powered risk assessment and smart notifications.

- Added AI Impact Assessment to evaluate update risk and classify as low, medium, or high.
- Introduced Smart Notification: auto-detects Telegram/Feishu channels and sends update reports and risk.
- New parameter: -NoNotify to skip sending notifications.
- Description and documentation updated to reflect new features.
- No code or logic for update mechanics changed.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions request access to local OpenClaw config files and perform system-level updates/restarts but the registry metadata declares no binaries, no config paths, and provides no scripts — the pieces don't line up.

dimensions.detail: The description says it's an OpenClaw auto-updater, which legitimately needs access to OpenClaw configuration and update tooling (npm, clawhub, ability to restart the gateway). However the registry metadata declares no required binaries, no required config paths, and no credentials — yet SKILL.md explicitly references PowerShell scripts, npm, clawhub, and files under ~/.openclaw. The declared requirements are incomplete and inconsistent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json, check system idle via Windows APIs, run npm -g update and clawhub update, send notifications to external messaging channels (Telegram/Feishu), and restart the gateway. These are broad actions touching local config files (which can contain secrets), network operations, and privileged system changes. The instructions also reference running scripts at scripts/self-updater.ps1, but no code files are present in the package.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec), which minimizes direct supply-chain risk. However SKILL.md expects a PowerShell script at scripts/self-updater.ps1 and external tools (npm, clawhub). Because no script is provided, the agent would either fail or attempt to recreate/execute commands directly — a behavioral gap that is suspicious and could lead to ad-hoc actions if the agent attempts to implement missing pieces.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Top-level metadata lists no required environment variables or config paths, but the runtime instructions require reading local config files (which likely contain messaging tokens, gateway credentials, and other secrets) and using npm and clawhub. The skill implicitly expects access to possibly-sensitive tokens inside ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json but doesn't declare or justify credential access in metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill performs privileged operations (global npm updates, updating all skills via clawhub, restarting the gateway). Although always:false (not force-installed), autonomous invocation is allowed by default; if granted runtime execution, the skill could perform disruptive system-level actions. The metadata does not surface these privileges explicitly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or enable this skill until the inconsistencies are resolved. Specific concerns to address before proceeding: (1) Provide a trusted source/homepage and the actual script files (scripts/self-updater.ps1) so you can inspect code; (2) Update registry metadata to declare required binaries (PowerShell, npm, clawhub) and the config paths it reads (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json); (3) Explain where messaging credentials live and why they are needed; (4) Prefer a dry-run mode and require explicit user consent for AutoUpdate and gateway restarts; (5) If you must test, run it in a restricted/sandboxed environment or inspect the script for network calls and credential handling first. Because it can update global packages and restart services, treat it as high-privilege and verify author and code before use.
